Under GST the tax is shared equally by the Central and the State governments, so in a tax invoice the rate of CGST is always equal to the rate of SGST and the two together make up the rate of GST.

Rate of GST = 12%

\(\therefore\) Rate of CGST = \(\frac{12}{2}\) = 6% and Rate of SGST = \(\frac{12}{2}\) = 6%

Ans. On these medicines the rate of CGST is 6% and the rate of SGST is 6%.

In a tax invoice the rate of CGST is always equal to the rate of SGST.

Rate of CGST = 9% \(\therefore\) Rate of SGST = 9%

Rate of GST = Rate of CGST + Rate of SGST = 9 + 9 = 18%

Ans. The rate of SGST is 9% and the rate of GST is 18%.

Taxable value of 2 tins = 2 \(\times\) 2800 = ₹ 5600

Rate of GST = 28% \(\therefore\) Rate of CGST = Rate of SGST = 14%

CGST = 14% of 5600 = \(\frac{14}{100} \times 5600\) = ₹ 784

\(\therefore\) SGST = CGST = ₹ 784

Ans. CGST charged in the tax invoice is ₹ 784 and SGST is ₹ 784.

Taxable value of the belt = ₹ 586, Rate of GST = 18%

GST = 18% of 586 = \(\frac{18}{100} \times 586\) = ₹ 105.48

Price for the customer = Taxable value + GST = 586 + 105.48 = ₹ 691.48

Ans. The customer gets the belt for ₹ 691.48.

Here the given price is the total value, that is the value WITH GST.

Rate of GST = 18%, so if the taxable value is ₹ 100 then the total value is ₹ 118, and the ratio \(\frac{Total value}{Taxable value}\) is constant.

Let the taxable value be ₹ \(x\).

\(\therefore \frac{x}{1770} = \frac{100}{118} \qquad \therefore x = \frac{1770 \times 100}{118}\) = ₹ 1500

\(\therefore\) Total GST = 1770 - 1500 = ₹ 270

\(\therefore\) CGST = SGST = \(\frac{270}{2}\) = ₹ 135

Ans. Taxable value of the toy car is ₹ 1500, CGST is ₹ 135 and SGST is ₹ 135.

(1) In a tax invoice the rate of SGST equals the rate of CGST \(\therefore\) Rate of SGST = 14%

(2) Rate of GST on AC = Rate of CGST + Rate of SGST = 14 + 14 = 28%

(3) ₹ 51,200 is the cost WITH GST. For a taxable value of ₹ 100 the total value is ₹ 128.

Let the taxable value be ₹ \(x\).

\(\therefore \frac{x}{51200} = \frac{100}{128} \qquad \therefore x = \frac{51200 \times 100}{128}\) = ₹ 40,000

(4) Total amount of GST = 51,200 - 40,000 = ₹ 11,200

(5) CGST = 14% of 40,000 = \(\frac{14}{100} \times 40000\) = ₹ 5600

(6) SGST = CGST = ₹ 5600

Ans. (1) 14% (2) 28% (3) ₹ 40,000 (4) ₹ 11,200 (5) ₹ 5600 (6) ₹ 5600.

Discount = 5% of 40,000 = \(\frac{5}{100} \times 40000\) = ₹ 2000

\(\therefore\) Taxable value of the washing machine = 40,000 - 2000 = ₹ 38,000

Rate of GST = 28% \(\therefore\) Rate of CGST = Rate of SGST = 14%

CGST = 14% of 38,000 = \(\frac{14}{100} \times 38000\) = ₹ 5320 \(\therefore\) SGST = ₹ 5320

\(\therefore\) Purchase price = 38,000 + 5320 + 5320 = ₹ 48,640

Ans. Prasad gets the washing machine for ₹ 48,640; the tax invoice shows CGST ₹ 5320 and SGST ₹ 5320.

Input tax (GST paid at the time of purchase) = ₹ 1,00,500 \(\therefore\) ITC = ₹ 1,00,500

Output tax (GST collected at the time of sale) = ₹ 1,22,500

GST payable = Output tax - ITC = 1,22,500 - 1,00,500 = ₹ 22,000

Ans. The GST payable by Chetana Stores is ₹ 22,000.

The GST paid at the time of purchase is the input tax, and the whole of it may be claimed as Input Tax Credit.

\(\therefore\) ITC to be claimed = ₹ 12,500

Output tax (collected on sale) = ₹ 14,750

GST payable = Output tax - ITC = 14,750 - 12,500 = ₹ 2250

Ans. The Input Tax Credit for Nazama is ₹ 12,500 and her payable GST is ₹ 2250.

Amir Enterprise : input tax = ₹ 3800, output tax = ₹ 4100

\(\therefore\) GST payable = 4100 - 3800 = ₹ 300

\(\therefore\) payable CGST = payable SGST = \(\frac{300}{2}\) = ₹ 150

Akbari Bros. : the GST of ₹ 4100 paid to Amir Enterprise is its input tax, and the ₹ 4500 collected from Mayank Food Corner is its output tax.

\(\therefore\) GST payable = 4500 - 4100 = ₹ 400

\(\therefore\) payable CGST = payable SGST = \(\frac{400}{2}\) = ₹ 200

Ans. Amir Enterprise : payable GST ₹ 300, payable CGST ₹ 150, payable SGST ₹ 150. Akbari Bros. : payable GST ₹ 400, payable CGST ₹ 200, payable SGST ₹ 200.

Input tax = 5% of 24,500 = \(\frac{5}{100} \times 24500\) = ₹ 1225 \(\therefore\) ITC = ₹ 1225

Output tax = 5% of 26,500 = \(\frac{5}{100} \times 26500\) = ₹ 1325

\(\therefore\) GST payable = Output tax - ITC = 1325 - 1225 = ₹ 100

Chandigarh is a Union Territory, so the tax is shared as CGST and UTGST instead of CGST and SGST.

\(\therefore\) CGST = UTGST = \(\frac{100}{2}\) = ₹ 50

Ans. Payable GST is ₹ 100, so CGST is ₹ 50 and UTGST is ₹ 50.

The tax invoice issued by M/s Beauty Products is the invoice for its SALE of ₹ 10,000, so the GST shown on it is charged on ₹ 10,000.

GST = 18% of 10,000 = \(\frac{18}{100} \times 10000\) = ₹ 1800

\(\therefore\) CGST = SGST = \(\frac{1800}{2}\) = ₹ 900

Ans. The tax invoice issued shows CGST ₹ 900 and SGST ₹ 900.

(The 18% GST on the purchase of ₹ 6000, that is ₹ 1080, is this firm's input tax. It appears on the supplier's invoice, not on the invoice issued here, and is claimed later as ITC.)

FV = ₹ 100, MV = ₹ 80, number of shares = 50, dividend = 20%.

Whatever the market value, the dividend is always reckoned on the Face Value.

Dividend per share = 20% of 100 = \(\frac{20}{100} \times 100\) = ₹ 20

\(\therefore\) Dividend income = 50 \(\times\) 20 = ₹ 1000

Sum invested = Number of shares \(\times\) MV = 50 \(\times\) 80 = ₹ 4000

Rate of return = \(\frac{Dividend income}{Sum invested}\) \(\times 100 = \frac{1000}{4000} \times 100 = 25\%\)

Ans. The rate of return on investment is 25%.

Company A : FV = ₹ 2, Premium = ₹ 18 \(\therefore\) MV = FV + Premium = 2 + 18 = ₹ 20

\(\therefore\) Investment in company A = 200 \(\times\) 20 = ₹ 4000

Company B : MV = ₹ 500 \(\therefore\) Investment in company B = 45 \(\times\) 500 = ₹ 22,500

Company C : MV = ₹ 10,540 \(\therefore\) Investment in company C = 1 \(\times\) 10,540 = ₹ 10,540

\(\therefore\) Total investment = 4000 + 22,500 + 10,540 = ₹ 37,040

Ans. Joseph's total investment is ₹ 37,040.

FV = ₹ 5, Premium = ₹ 20 \(\therefore\) MV = FV + Premium = 5 + 20 = ₹ 25

Number of shares = \(\frac{Sum invested}{MV}\) \(= \frac{20000}{25} = 800\)

Ans. Smt. Deshpande will get 800 shares for ₹ 20,000.

FV = ₹ 100, MV = ₹ 120, number of shares = 150, dividend = 7%.

Dividend per share = 7% of 100 = ₹ 7

\(\therefore\) Dividend income = 150 \(\times\) 7 = ₹ 1050

Sum invested = 150 \(\times\) 120 = ₹ 18,000

Rate of return = \(\frac{Dividend income}{Sum invested}\) \(\times 100 = \frac{1050}{18000} \times 100 = \frac{35}{6} = 5.83\%\) (approx.)

Ans. The rate of return on his investment is 5.83%.

The face value of both the shares is the same; take FV = ₹ 100 for each.

Company A : dividend = 16% \(\therefore\) dividend per share = 16% of 100 = ₹ 16, MV = ₹ 80

\(\therefore\) Rate of return = \(\frac{16}{80} \times 100 = 20\%\)

Company B : dividend = 20% \(\therefore\) dividend per share = 20% of 100 = ₹ 20, MV = ₹ 120

\(\therefore\) Rate of return = \(\frac{20}{120} \times 100 = 16.67\%\) (approx.)

20% > 16.67%, so every rupee invested in company A earns more.

Ans. Investment in Company A is more profitable.

Brokerage is always calculated on the Market value of the share.

Brokerage = 0.3% of 200 = \(\frac{0.3}{100} \times 200\) = ₹ 0.60

At the time of buying, the brokerage is ADDED to the market value.

\(\therefore\) Purchase value of the share = MV + Brokerage = 200 + 0.60 = ₹ 200.60

Ans. The purchase value of the share is ₹ 200.60.

Brokerage = 0.1% of 1000 = \(\frac{0.1}{100} \times 1000\) = ₹ 1

At the time of selling, the brokerage is DEDUCTED from the market value.

\(\therefore\) Amount received = MV - Brokerage = 1000 - 1 = ₹ 999

Ans. The amount received after the sale is ₹ 999.

Row 1 (buy) : Total value = 100 \(\times\) 45 = ₹ 4500

Brokerage = 0.2% of 4500 = \(\frac{0.2}{100} \times 4500\) = ₹ 9

CGST = 9% of 9 = ₹ 0.81 \(\therefore\) SGST = ₹ 0.81

On a purchase the brokerage and the tax on it are ADDED.

\(\therefore\) Total value of shares = 4500 + 9 + 0.81 + 0.81 = ₹ 4510.62

Row 2 (sell) : Total value = 75 \(\times\) 200 = ₹ 15,000

Brokerage = 0.2% of 15,000 = ₹ 30

CGST = 9% of 30 = ₹ 2.70 \(\therefore\) SGST = ₹ 2.70

On a sale the brokerage and the tax on it are DEDUCTED.

\(\therefore\) Total value of shares = 15,000 - 30 - 2.70 - 2.70 = ₹ 14,964.60

MV = ₹ 50, rate of brokerage = 0.2%, rate of GST on brokerage = 18%.

Brokerage per share = 0.2% of 50 = \(\frac{0.2}{100} \times 50\) = ₹ 0.10

GST per share on brokerage = 18% of 0.10 = ₹ 0.018

At the time of selling, both the brokerage and the GST on it are deducted from the MV.

\(\therefore\) Selling price per share = 50 - 0.10 - 0.018 = ₹ 49.882

\(\therefore\) Number of shares sold = \(\frac{Amount received}{Selling price per share}\) \(= \frac{4988.20}{49.882} = 100\)

Ans. Smt. Desai sold 100 shares.

Purchase : FV = ₹ 50, Premium = ₹ 100 \(\therefore\) MV = 50 + 100 = ₹ 150

Cost of 200 shares = 200 \(\times\) 150 = ₹ 30,000, and the brokerage on this trade is ₹ 20.

\(\therefore\) Total amount paid = 30,000 + 20 = ₹ 30,020

Dividend : 50% of FV = \(\frac{50}{100} \times 50\) = ₹ 25 per share

\(\therefore\) Dividend received = 200 \(\times\) 25 = ₹ 5000

First sale : 100 shares at a discount of ₹ 10 \(\therefore\) MV = 50 - 10 = ₹ 40

Value = 100 \(\times\) 40 = ₹ 4000, less brokerage ₹ 20 \(\therefore\) amount received = ₹ 3980

Second sale : the remaining 100 shares at a premium of ₹ 75 \(\therefore\) MV = 50 + 75 = ₹ 125

Value = 100 \(\times\) 125 = ₹ 12,500, less brokerage ₹ 20 \(\therefore\) amount received = ₹ 12,480

\(\therefore\) Total income = 5000 + 3980 + 12,480 = ₹ 21,460

Total amount paid = ₹ 30,020, and 30,020 > 21,460, so there is a loss.

Loss = 30,020 - 21,460 = ₹ 8560

Ans. Mr. D'souza incurred a loss of ₹ 8560.

Discount = 10% of 25,000 = \(\frac{10}{100} \times 25000\) = ₹ 2500

\(\therefore\) Discounted price, that is the taxable value = 25,000 - 2500 = ₹ 22,500

Rate of GST = 28% \(\therefore\) Rate of CGST = Rate of SGST = 14%

CGST = 14% of 22,500 = \(\frac{14}{100} \times 22500\) = ₹ 3150 \(\therefore\) SGST = ₹ 3150

\(\therefore\) Total amount shown in the tax invoice = 22,500 + 3150 + 3150 = ₹ 28,800

Ans. Total bill is ₹ 28,800; CGST is ₹ 3150 and SGST is ₹ 3150.

Discount = 5% of 1000 = ₹ 50

\(\therefore\) Remaining (taxable) amount = 1000 - 50 = ₹ 950

GST = 5% of 950 = \(\frac{5}{100} \times 950\) = ₹ 47.50

\(\therefore\) Purchase price for the customer = 950 + 47.50 = ₹ 997.50

Ans. The purchase price of the dress for the customer is ₹ 997.50.

Surat and Rajkot are both in Gujarat, so this is trading WITHIN one state. The tax is therefore charged as CGST and SGST, and the two together make up the 5% GST.

Taxable value = ₹ 2.5 lacs = ₹ 2,50,000

GST = 5% of 2,50,000 = \(\frac{5}{100} \times 250000\) = ₹ 12,500

Ans. The trader in Rajkot pays ₹ 12,500 as GST (CGST ₹ 6250 + SGST ₹ 6250).

Input tax = 5% of 85,000 = \(\frac{5}{100} \times 85000\) = ₹ 4250 \(\therefore\) ITC = ₹ 4250

Output tax = 5% of 90,000 = \(\frac{5}{100} \times 90000\) = ₹ 4500

\(\therefore\) GST payable = Output tax - ITC = 4500 - 4250 = ₹ 250

Ans. The ITC of Smt. Malhotra is ₹ 4250 and the GST payable by her is ₹ 250.

Output tax = 18% of 64,500 = \(\frac{18}{100} \times 64500\) = ₹ 11,610

The GST of ₹ 1550 the company paid for laundry services and uniforms is its input tax, and the whole of it is available as credit.

\(\therefore\) ITC = ₹ 1550

GST payable = Output tax - ITC = 11,610 - 1550 = ₹ 10,060

\(\therefore\) payable CGST = payable SGST = \(\frac{10060}{2}\) = ₹ 5030

Ans. The Input Tax Credit is ₹ 1550; payable CGST is ₹ 5030 and payable SGST is ₹ 5030.

₹ 84,000 is the value WITH GST. Rate of GST = 12%, so for a taxable value of ₹ 100 the total value is ₹ 112.

Let the taxable value be ₹ \(x\).

\(\therefore \frac{x}{84000} = \frac{100}{112} \qquad \therefore x = \frac{84000 \times 100}{112}\) = ₹ 75,000

\(\therefore\) Total GST = 84,000 - 75,000 = ₹ 9000

\(\therefore\) CGST = SGST = \(\frac{9000}{2}\) = ₹ 4500

Ans. The taxable value of the set is ₹ 75,000; the dealer charged central GST ₹ 4500 and state GST ₹ 4500.

Rate of GST = 18% \(\therefore\) Rate of CGST = Rate of SGST = 9%

Computation of GST in the tax invoices of sales :

Wholesaler's tax invoice (sale to the retailer, taxable amount ₹ 1,80,000) :

CGST = 9% of 1,80,000 = ₹ 16,200 and SGST = ₹ 16,200

Retailer's tax invoice (sale to the customer, taxable amount ₹ 2,20,000) :

CGST = 9% of 2,20,000 = ₹ 19,800 and SGST = ₹ 19,800

Payable tax :

Wholesaler's input CGST = 9% of 1,50,000 = ₹ 13,500

\(\therefore\) payable CGST = 16,200 - 13,500 = ₹ 2700 and payable SGST = ₹ 2700

Retailer's input CGST = ₹ 16,200 (paid to the wholesaler)

\(\therefore\) payable CGST = 19,800 - 16,200 = ₹ 3600 and payable SGST = ₹ 3600

Ans. Wholesaler's tax invoice shows CGST ₹ 16,200 and SGST ₹ 16,200; retailer's tax invoice shows CGST ₹ 19,800 and SGST ₹ 19,800. The wholesaler pays CGST ₹ 2700 and SGST ₹ 2700, and the retailer pays CGST ₹ 3600 and SGST ₹ 3600.

Thane and Vasai are both in Maharashtra, so this is trading within one state and the tax is charged as CGST and SGST.

Rate of GST = 28% \(\therefore\) Rate of CGST = Rate of SGST = 14%

(1) Anna Patil's tax invoice, taxable value ₹ 14,000 :

CGST = 14% of 14,000 = \(\frac{14}{100} \times 14000\) = ₹ 1960 \(\therefore\) SGST = ₹ 1960

(2) Shopkeeper's tax invoice, taxable value ₹ 16,800 :

CGST = 14% of 16,800 = \(\frac{14}{100} \times 16800\) = ₹ 2352 \(\therefore\) SGST = ₹ 2352

(3) The shopkeeper's input tax is the CGST ₹ 1960 and SGST ₹ 1960 he paid to Anna Patil.

\(\therefore\) payable CGST = 2352 - 1960 = ₹ 392 and payable SGST = 2352 - 1960 = ₹ 392

Ans. (1) CGST ₹ 1960 and SGST ₹ 1960 (2) CGST ₹ 2352 and SGST ₹ 2352 (3) payable CGST ₹ 392 and payable SGST ₹ 392.

[Textbook note: the printed answer to part (3) reads "Manufacturer to distributor B2B, distributor to retailer B2B, retailer to customer B2C". The chain given in this question begins with a WHOLESALER and contains no manufacturer, so the first party is misnamed in the key. The classification itself - invoices I and II are B2B and invoice III is B2C - is correct.]

Rate of GST = 12% \(\therefore\) Rate of CGST = Rate of SGST = 6%

Tax invoice I (wholesaler to distributor), taxable value ₹ 5000 :

CGST = 6% of 5000 = ₹ 300, SGST = ₹ 300, invoice value = 5000 + 600 = ₹ 5600

Tax invoice II (distributor to retailer), taxable value ₹ 6000 :

CGST = 6% of 6000 = ₹ 360, SGST = ₹ 360, invoice value = 6000 + 720 = ₹ 6720

Tax invoice III (retailer to consumer), taxable value ₹ 6500 :

CGST = 6% of 6500 = ₹ 390, SGST = ₹ 390, invoice value = 6500 + 780 = ₹ 7280

(1) Each trader pays the tax he collected less the tax he paid at the time of purchase.

| Person | Payable CGST (₹) | Payable SGST (₹) | Payable GST (₹) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Wholesaler | 300 | 300 | 600 |
| Distributor | 360 - 300 = 60 | 60 | 120 |
| Retailer | 390 - 360 = 30 | 30 | 60 |
| Total Tax | 390 | 390 | 780 |

(2) At the end the consumer pays the retailer's invoice value, that is ₹ 7280.

(3) The wholesaler, the distributor and the retailer are all registered dealers, so tax invoice I and tax invoice II are B2B. The consumer is not a dealer, so tax invoice III is B2C.

Ans. (1) Total payable CGST ₹ 390, SGST ₹ 390, GST ₹ 780, split as in the table above (2) ₹ 7280 (3) invoices I and II are B2B, invoice III is B2C.

FV = ₹ 100, MV = ₹ 180, number of shares = 50, dividend = 40%.

FV = ₹ 100 and the shares are sold at a discount of ₹ 30.

\(\therefore\) MV = FV - Discount = 100 - 30 = ₹ 70

Amount received = Number of shares \(\times\) MV = 300 \(\times\) 70 = ₹ 21,000

Ans. ₹ 21,000 is received. (No brokerage is mentioned in this question, so none is deducted.)

The number of shares depends on the market value, not on the face value.

MV = ₹ 120

Number of shares = \(\frac{Sum invested}{MV}\) \(= \frac{60000}{120} = 500\)

Ans. 500 shares are received for ₹ 60,000.

Purchase : MV = ₹ 100 and the sum invested in the shares is ₹ 10,200

\(\therefore\) Number of shares = \(\frac{10200}{100} = 102\)

Brokerage = 0.1% of 10,200 = ₹ 10.20

\(\therefore\) Total amount paid = 10,200 + 10.20 = ₹ 10,210.20

First sale : 60 shares at MV ₹ 125 \(\therefore\) value = 60 \(\times\) 125 = ₹ 7500

Brokerage = 0.1% of 7500 = ₹ 7.50 \(\therefore\) amount received = 7500 - 7.50 = ₹ 7492.50

Second sale : the remaining 102 - 60 = 42 shares at MV ₹ 90 \(\therefore\) value = 42 \(\times\) 90 = ₹ 3780

Brokerage = 0.1% of 3780 = ₹ 3.78 \(\therefore\) amount received = 3780 - 3.78 = ₹ 3776.22

\(\therefore\) Total amount received = 7492.50 + 3776.22 = ₹ 11,268.72

As 11,268.72 > 10,210.20, she made a profit.

Profit = 11,268.72 - 10,210.20 = ₹ 1058.52

Ans. Smt. Mita Agrawal made a profit of ₹ 1058.52.

FV = ₹ 100 for both the shares.

Company A : dividend = 12% \(\therefore\) dividend per share = ₹ 12, MV = ₹ 132

\(\therefore\) Rate of return = \(\frac{12}{132} \times 100 = 9.09\%\) (approx.)

Company B : dividend = 16% \(\therefore\) dividend per share = ₹ 16, MV = ₹ 144

\(\therefore\) Rate of return = \(\frac{16}{144} \times 100 = 11.11\%\) (approx.)

11.11% > 9.09%

Ans. Investment in Company B is more profitable, as the returns are more.

MV = ₹ 50, rate of brokerage = 0.2%, rate of GST on brokerage = 18%.

Brokerage per share = 0.2% of 50 = \(\frac{0.2}{100} \times 50\) = ₹ 0.10

GST per share on brokerage = 18% of 0.10 = ₹ 0.018

At the time of buying, both are added to the market value.

\(\therefore\) Cost of one share = MV + Brokerage + GST = 50 + 0.10 + 0.018 = ₹ 50.118

\(\therefore\) Number of shares = \(\frac{Sum invested}{Cost of one share}\) \(= \frac{50118}{50.118} = 1000\)

Ans. 1000 shares were purchased for ₹ 50,118.

Purchase : number of shares = 22, MV = ₹ 660

\(\therefore\) Sum invested = 22 \(\times\) 660 = ₹ 14,520

Brokerage = 0.1% of 14,520 = ₹ 14.52

\(\therefore\) Total amount paid = 14,520 + 14.52 = ₹ 14,534.52

Dividend : 20% of FV = 20% of 100 = ₹ 20 per share

\(\therefore\) Dividend received = 22 \(\times\) 20 = ₹ 440

Sale : MV = ₹ 650 \(\therefore\) value = 22 \(\times\) 650 = ₹ 14,300

Brokerage = 0.1% of 14,300 = ₹ 14.30 \(\therefore\) amount received = 14,300 - 14.30 = ₹ 14,285.70

\(\therefore\) Total income = 440 + 14,285.70 = ₹ 14,725.70

As 14,725.70 > 14,534.52, there is a profit.

Profit = 14,725.70 - 14,534.52 = ₹ 191.18

Percent profit = \(\frac{Profit}{Total amount paid}\) \(\times 100 = \frac{191.18}{14534.52} \times 100 = 1.32\%\)
